title: CFTC Regulation CTX/CAM Proposal-to-Final and Operation Baseline
purpose: Preserve thirty stable comparison dimensions across the announcement, public ANPRM, later NPRM, final rule and operating evidence without overwriting earlier states.
scope_boundary: Announcement-level architecture and explicitly unknown fields only. The public ANPRM text, numbered questions, proposed CFR text, economics, final rule and CAM operation were not available at the cutoff.

rulemaking.title: Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets

authority_rule: The Federal Register ANPRM and any Commission-approved public text will control the proposal. Release 9307-26 and the chairman's statement establish announcement-level architecture only. Existing DCM rules, Bitnomial filings and official comments are comparators or stakeholder positions, not Regulation CTX/CAM text.

comparison_contract.instruction: Never overwrite announcement_baseline. When the ANPRM appears, populate anprm_public_text for every provision. Later populate nprm, final_rule and operation separately. Add a provision only for a material object with no earlier counterpart.
minimum_later_stage_evidence: controlling release, Federal Register or Commission order
exact CFR, form, designation, rulebook or product reference
effective and compliance dates where applicable
named entity and operating receipt when carrying an operation claim

layers.label: Instrument, authority and lineage
layers.question: What legal object is this, which authority supports it and how does it relate to AF66 and later stages?

layers.label: Transaction and asset perimeter
layers.question: Which crypto assets and transactions enter Regulation CTX?

layers.label: Venue designation and product listing
layers.question: What is a CAM, who can become one and how are CTXs listed?

layers.label: Access, intermediation and financing
layers.question: Who may access, introduce, carry and finance customers?

layers.label: Clearing and financial resources
layers.question: What must be cleared, by whom, with which collateral and default resources?

layers.label: Custody, customer property and failure
layers.question: Who controls assets and keys, which property regime applies and what happens in insolvency?

layers.label: Market integrity, surveillance and records
layers.question: What data, controls and official records make the market supervisable?

layers.label: Settlement, finality and resilience
layers.question: How do asset and cash legs settle, fail, pause, correct and recover?

layers.label: SEC, state, AML and other boundaries
layers.question: Which legal regimes remain outside or beside the CAM framework?

layers.label: Governance, conflicts, enforcement and remedy
layers.question: How are integrated functions governed and how are violations and customer losses remedied?

layers.label: Economics, burden and alternatives
layers.question: Who bears costs and risks, which alternatives are considered and what evidence supports the analysis?

layers.label: Comment, effectiveness and operation
layers.question: When does proposal become rule, designation, product and observed market operation?

provisions.label: Instrument type
provisions.announcement_baseline: The CFTC describes the October 5 object as an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking used to solicit public input before potential future rulemaking.
provisions.later_question: Does the Federal Register object use the same instrument label and does it contain contemplated text, proposed text or questions only?

provisions.label: RIN and AF66 relationship
provisions.announcement_baseline: OIRA identifies RIN 3038-AF80. No official source links AF80 to RIN 3038-AF66, Blockchain and Digital Assets.
provisions.later_question: Does the public text link, supersede, split or preserve AF66?

provisions.label: Regulation CTX and Regulation CAM
provisions.announcement_baseline: The CFTC names two contemplated regimes: Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets.
provisions.later_question: Are the regimes separate CFR parts, joined subparts, interpretations, designation conditions or exemptive frameworks?

provisions.label: Section 2(c)(2)(D) transaction hook
provisions.announcement_baseline: CTXs are retail commodity transactions involving crypto assets under CEA section 2(c)(2)(D), generally offered to retail on a leveraged, margined or financed basis subject to statutory exceptions.
provisions.later_question: How does the text define offered, leverage, margin, financing, retail customer, person acting in concert and actual delivery?

provisions.label: Crypto asset eligibility
provisions.announcement_baseline: The chairman identifies non-security crypto assets such as bitcoin and ether as the intended commodity-side class, but no CAM eligibility test is public.
provisions.later_question: What non-security, network, liquidity, manipulation, disclosure, governance, supply, custody or exclusion tests govern each listed asset?

provisions.label: CAM legal status
provisions.announcement_baseline: CAM is described as a purpose-built subcategory of designated contract market registration for CTXs.
provisions.later_question: Is CAM a new designation class, elective DCM subtype, limited-purpose DCM, exemptive overlay or combination?

provisions.label: Elective route and mandatory perimeter
provisions.announcement_baseline: The chairman describes a purpose-fit option and says the CFTC cannot require all crypto assets to trade on CFTC venues without Congress.
provisions.later_question: Does offering leverage trigger registration for a platform, and can fully paid orders share the same CAM order book?

provisions.label: CTX listing and Part 40 route
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not disclose whether CTXs use Rule 40.2 self-certification, Rule 40.3 approval, asset certification, SEC consultation or another route.
provisions.later_question: What rule and product filings are required before a CAM lists a CTX?

provisions.label: Retail leveraged, margined or financed trading
provisions.announcement_baseline: CAMs are intended to offer covered retail crypto trading on a leveraged, margined or financed basis.
provisions.later_question: What leverage limits, disclosures, liquidation rules and customer eligibility conditions apply?

provisions.label: Direct access, FCM and IB routes
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not choose between direct retail access, FCM/IB intermediation, self-clearing membership or multiple routes.
provisions.later_question: Who opens and carries the account, accepts funds, introduces orders and bears customer-facing duties?

provisions.label: Financing provider and lending perimeter
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not identify whether financing may be provided by the CAM, FCM, DCO, affiliate, third party or another regulated person.
provisions.later_question: Who may lend cash or crypto and which federal/state capital, licensing, priority and liquidation rules apply?

provisions.label: DCO clearing requirement
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not say whether DCO clearing is mandatory, optional, exempted or limited to the financing obligation.
provisions.later_question: What is novated or guaranteed after prompt asset transfer, and who becomes counterparty?

provisions.label: Capital, liquidity and default resources
provisions.announcement_baseline: No CAM minimum capital, liquidity, insurance, guaranty fund, default resources or wind-down standard is announced.
provisions.later_question: Which resources sit at CAM, FCM, lender, DCO and custodian, and which loss each resource covers?

provisions.label: Custody, wallets and key control
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not identify the custodian, key controller, wallet standard, self-custody route or fork/airdrop treatment.
provisions.later_question: May the CAM, FCM, DCO, affiliate, bank, trust company or customer control the assets and keys?

provisions.label: Customer-property and insolvency regime
provisions.announcement_baseline: The CFTC announces consumer-protection objectives but no section 4d, Part 190, trust, bailment, UCC Article 8 or contractual property mechanism.
provisions.later_question: Which assets enter a protected estate, which claims remain unsecured and which remedy applies after platform, FCM, lender, DCO or custodian failure?

provisions.label: Rehypothecation and reuse
provisions.announcement_baseline: No rule for lender or intermediary reuse of customer crypto or collateral is announced.
provisions.later_question: Is reuse prohibited, capped to financed exposure, disclosed and consented, or allowed only through a separately regulated lender?

provisions.label: Cross-venue and on/off-chain surveillance
provisions.announcement_baseline: The CFTC seeks input on preventing abusive practices but does not disclose required on-chain, off-chain, identity, wallet, beneficial-owner, oracle or cross-venue data.
provisions.later_question: What data must the CAM obtain, retain, share and use to detect manipulation, wash trading, spoofing and related-party activity?

provisions.label: Order, trade, position, asset and customer records
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not identify which order, trade, wallet, custody, financing, liquidation, customer, beneficial-owner and correction records are official.
provisions.later_question: Which legal entity owns each record and how must it be reproduced during network or venue outage?

provisions.label: Asset delivery, cash settlement and legal finality
provisions.announcement_baseline: No rule is announced for technical confirmation, possession/control, legal discharge, bank or stablecoin cash legs, reversal, fork or failed settlement.
provisions.later_question: What completes each leg and who may correct or reverse an erroneous or contested transfer?

provisions.label: 24/7 operation and recovery
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not address staffing, bank-hour gaps, collateral calls, liquidity, cyber, key loss, oracle failure, market pauses, forks or recovery.
provisions.later_question: What minimum continuous-operation, incident, emergency and recovery controls apply to CAM and connected entities?

provisions.label: SEC classification and mixed-market boundary
provisions.announcement_baseline: The chairman relies on the March 2026 SEC-CFTC interpretation but does not disclose CAM consultation, security-futures, mixed-platform or investment-contract procedures.
provisions.later_question: Who decides asset and transaction status, and how do dual or mixed registrations work?

provisions.label: State-law and preemption boundary
provisions.announcement_baseline: The chairman describes a single federal market-regulatory scheme; no preemption text is public for exchange, lending, trust/custody, money transmission, UCC, consumer protection or insolvency law.
provisions.later_question: Which state duties are displaced, preserved or duplicated?

provisions.label: AML, sanctions and tax joins
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not describe FinCEN, BSA, OFAC, Travel Rule, IRS or tax-reporting duties for CAM, affiliates or wallets.
provisions.later_question: Which entity owns identity, suspicious-activity, sanctions-screening, travel-data and tax-reporting duties?

provisions.label: Vertical integration
provisions.announcement_baseline: The announcement does not say which listing, execution, lending, custody, settlement, proprietary and affiliate functions may sit in one entity or group.
provisions.later_question: What legal, governance, personnel, data and financial-resource separation or independent oversight is required?

provisions.label: Fees, ownership and trading conflicts
provisions.announcement_baseline: No rule is announced for listing fees, rebates, spread economics, affiliate trading, market making, token ownership, issuer relationships or governance conflicts.
provisions.later_question: Which conflicts are prohibited, disclosed, firewalled, independently approved or monitored?

provisions.label: Examination, discipline, enforcement and customer remedy
provisions.announcement_baseline: The release names prevention of abusive practices but does not disclose examination, NFA/SRO, CAM discipline, restitution, error-correction or asset-return mechanisms.
provisions.later_question: Which actor investigates, adjudicates, corrects, pays and returns property after violation or loss?

provisions.label: Economic analysis, burdens and alternatives
provisions.announcement_baseline: OIRA classified the prerule as not economically significant. No public cost-benefit, PRA, IRFA, affected-entity, alternative or burden analysis is available.
provisions.later_question: What populations, costs, benefits, risks, small-entity effects, data limits and alternatives does the ANPRM identify?

provisions.label: Federal Register and comment clock
provisions.announcement_baseline: Comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication; publication and calendar close dates were not public by the cutoff.
provisions.later_question: What are the publication date, docket, close date, extensions, meetings and supplemental materials?

provisions.label: Effectiveness, compliance and transition
provisions.announcement_baseline: No rule, effective date, compliance date, transition, grandfathering or provisional status exists.
provisions.later_question: What later-stage dates and transition rules control each entity, product and existing arrangement?

provisions.label: CAM designation, CTX listing and observed operation
provisions.announcement_baseline: No CAM application or designation, CAM rulebook, CTX filing, participant, customer account, funding, trade, volume, incident or remedy is established.
provisions.later_question: Which named entity reaches each operating gate and what public receipt proves it?
